notes: Almonty is incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act. Shareholders approved moving to Delaware in Feb 2025, but the move hasn't been completed (the 2025 annual information form says it is still under consideration). It moved its headquarters from Toronto to Dillon, Montana in April 2026 and files 6-K reports as a foreign private issuer, with IFRS accounts in Canadian dollars.
Listing: Nasdaq Capital Market (ALM) since a US$90M IPO in July 2025. It voluntarily delisted from the TSX on Jul 31, 2026 and from the ASX on Sep 1, 2026; a Frankfurt quote (ALI1) remains.

Sangdong (South Korea) got its final operating certificates on Sep 17 and produced its first tungsten concentrate in 33 years in late September. The first cargo is booked for Oct 24. Phase I targets ~640,000 tonnes of ore a year. Phase II (up to 1.2M t/yr, potentially over 460,000 MTU a year) is under way and due in 2027.

Offtake: the Jul 14, 2026 amendment with Global Tungsten & Powders (part of Plansee, which is also a major shareholder) adds six years, raises contracted volumes 40% and improves pricing by about 6.3%. S&P says about 90% of Phase I output is committed for 21 years.
The headline 'net income' and the 125% TTM net margin come from fair-value swings on the convertible notes and capped calls, not from mining.
Joined the Russell 1000 and Russell 3000 on Jun 29, 2026.

catalysts.event: First Sangdong concentrate cargo (booked): the first proof of Phase I sales
Q3 2026 results: the first quarter with Sangdong production, plus the tungsten price effect
Platts' proposed non-China tungsten concentrate and APT price assessments (CIF US ports) take effect
DFARS 252.225-7052 bars US defense purchases of tungsten from China, Russia, Iran and North Korea, down to the mining stage
Sangdong Phase II completes (up to 1.2M t/yr of ore; Metso mills ordered); a tungsten oxide facility in Korea, Gentung (Montana) and the Panasqueira extension run in parallel
Buyback: up to 14.4M shares or US$300M; 2,914,739 shares (~US$48M) bought by Sep 29; an automatic purchase plan is planned
Delaware domestication: shareholders approved it in Feb 2025; the company says it remains under consideration and it hasn't been completed

bull.text: Ex-China tungsten is short: S&P estimates a ~21,000-tonne non-China supply gap in 2026, and APT rose from $83/kg to $340/kg WO3 between January and July
Sangdong is now producing, and Phase II is fully funded from C$1.23B in cash
Long-term offtake with Plansee/GTP (40% more volume, ~6.3% better pricing) and US defense sourcing rules from 2027 support Western-origin pricing
On forward numbers (14.7x P/E, 5.4x sales) it is cheap if the ramp delivers, and the company is buying back its own shares

bear.text: Commodity price risk: APT is already down from ~US$3,075 to ~US$2,700, and the bull case depends on China's export-control premium lasting
Execution: Sangdong only restarted in September after 33 years shut, the first cargo hasn't shipped yet, and Phase II still has to be built by 2027
Dilution and leverage: share count +44.1% YoY, and US$800M of converts due 2031 can add shares
Reported profit is distorted: Q2's C$181.8M net income is mostly non-cash derivative gains, and figures are in CAD while the stock trades in USD

runContext.title: What kind of company this is, and does it belong on Risk It?
runContext.summary: ALM is a commodity producer: a tungsten miner whose revenue moves with the APT price. It is not a crypto miner. Risk It's written rules only exclude bitcoin/crypto miners, SPACs, mortgage REITs and Growth names, so it qualifies. Early Inflection would exclude it, because that screen drops commodity producers by Nasdaq industry ('Other Metals and Minerals').

listContext.method: Risk It is a maximum-growth screen that accepts much higher risk. We start from every US-listed stock in the StockAnalysis / S&P Global screener and keep those with a market cap over $300M, at least $10M a day of average trading volume, TTM revenue of $50M or more, coverage from 5+ analysts with a price target, and growth that is current and expected to continue (latest-quarter revenue up 15%+ YoY and consensus revenue growth of 15%+ this fiscal year and 10%+ next). Mortgage REITs, SPACs and anything already in Growth Picks are excluded. Each stock is scored 0–100: TTM revenue growth up to 40

gradeNote: Growth (A-) is driven by TTM revenue +205%; there is no 3-yr EPS forecast. Value (D) is held down by a trailing EV/sales of 53x on pre-Sangdong revenue, despite a 14.7x forward P/E. Momentum (D): a strong year (+70%, +54 pts vs SPY) but −24% over 6 months and −20% over 3 months as tungsten prices came off their high. Profitability (C+) is flattered: the 125% net margin comes from non-cash derivative and warrant gains, while the operating margin is 5.2% and the FCF margin −64%. Margins and growth use StockAnalysis TTM figures (US$ conversions of C$ statements; the ratios are unaffected by currency).
